question: A 16-year-old male is brought to the clinic by his mother for the complaints of fever, nonproductive cough, fatigue, lack of appetite, and sore throat for the past 2 months.  Several other students at his high school have had similar symptoms. Physical exam shows a whitish membrane in his oropharynx, bilateral enlarged cervical lymphadenopathy, and mild splenomegaly.  Which of the following tests is most likely to diagnose his condition.?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fever, nonproductive cough, fatigue, lack of appetite, sore throat" -> "Possible infectious etiology" -> "Consider infectious mononucleosis" -> 70% CHAIN: "Whitish membrane in oropharynx, bilateral enlarged cervical lymphadenopathy, mild splenomegaly" -> "Clinical features suggestive of infectious mononucleosis" -> "Consider Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection" -> 80% CHAIN: "Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection" -> "Common cause of infectious mononucleosis" -> "Monospot test" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely test to diagnose the 16-year-old male's condition presenting with symptoms suggestive of infectious mononucleosis, including whitish membrane in oropharynx, bilateral enlarged cervical lymphadenopathy, and mild splenomegaly, is the Monospot test. This test is commonly used for diagnosing Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection, a common cause of infectious mononucleosis.
analysis: The most likely diagnosis based on the symptoms described is infectious mononucleosis, commonly caused by the Epstein-Barr virus. The presence of a whitish membrane in the oropharynx, bilateral enlarged cervical lymphadenopathy, mild splenomegaly, and the history of contact with other students with similar symptoms are suggestive of this viral infection.
